title: The #1 Factor That Will Drive Gold & Silver Prices | Jeff Christian
speaker: Jeff Christian (CPM Group), interviewed by Lis

macro_themes.view: Not worried by yield levels themselves but by the reason: debt everywhere; doesn't see rates coming down sharply, they could rise.
Expects a recession in the industrialized world, timing uncertain, driven by rates plus geopolitical factors (US-Iran war, Russia-Ukraine, trade deterioration).
The Fed can stop the bleeding but only fiscal policy cures the disease; governments have no incentive to fix it.
Secular rise in gold/silver investment demand on economic, fiscal and political malaise will keep prices high; gold investment demand may hit a record this year.
Huge margins (gold AISC ~$1,800) will spur more supply and weigh on prices in maybe ~5 years.
Solar silver use peaked and will fall ~40% over 10 years, offset by EVs, AI, electronics, substitution for PGMs.

calls.reason: Investment demand, driven by economic/fiscal/political malaise, will keep trumping weak fabrication demand and rising supply; gold stays high. Notes gold ~30% off its peak and ~$4,000+.
calls.quote: we think that the investment demand will continue to trump the fabrication demand. And so you're going to see the gold and silver prices stay …

calls.reason: Investment demand (financial plus affordable alternative to gold) and growing electrification/EV/AI fabrication demand are long-term positive; mine supply incentive may weigh in ~5 years.
calls.quote: both of them are positive on the long-term basis for gold for silver

calls.reason: Gold AISC ~$1,800 vs very high prices gives tremendous margins; producers should be extremely profitable for the next few years.
calls.quote: in the meantime the gold producers should be extremely pro profitable

calls.reason: Rising debt across sovereign, corporate and consumer sectors is pushing rates up; he does not see rates falling sharply.
calls.quote: I don't see interest rates coming down sharply and you know I I think that they could rise
